speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, everyone, and thank you for coming to our workshop, Building with Perception Agents.
zh: 大家好，感谢各位来参加我们的工作坊「Building with Perception Agents(构建感知智能体)」。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Emil Bazel.
zh: 我叫 Emil Bazel。

speaker: Unknown
en: I lead a team of solutions architects within Amazon AGI Lab.
zh: 我在 Amazon AGI Lab 内部领导一个解决方案架构师团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our team is focused on two things.
zh: 我们团队专注于两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is working with some of our earliest adopter customers who want to work with some of our early models and products.
zh: 第一是与一些最早期的采用者客户合作，他们想使用我们的一些早期模型和产品，

speaker: Unknown
en: to help them get into production.
zh: 帮助他们进入生产环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second part is closing the feedback loop from our customer engagements, building evals for our research team to train our models on, and bringing product and engineering feedback to those teams as well.
zh: 第二部分是打通客户合作的反馈闭环，为我们的研究团队构建评测（evals）以用于训练模型，同时也把产品和工程方面的反馈带给那些团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm joined by one of our stellar solutions architects, Shruti Arora, who's gonna be running the workshop today.
zh: 和我一起来的还有我们一位非常出色的解决方案架构师 Shruti Arora，她今天将主持这个工作坊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a bit about what we're gonna be talking about today.
zh: 简单介绍一下我们今天要讲的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll be giving a quick overview of the Amazon AGI Lab and talking about the first product that we shipped last year, Amazon Nova Act, and then we'll get into perception agents, and that's what the focus of today's workshop is, and then we'll get into the workshop.
zh: 我会先快速概述一下 Amazon AGI Lab，谈谈我们去年发布的第一个产品 Amazon Nova Act，然后进入感知智能体——这是今天工作坊的重点——之后我们就进入工作坊环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a bit about the lab.
zh: 先简单介绍一下这个实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are a frontier research and product team that combines startup speed with the scale and the resources of Amazon.
zh: 我们是一个前沿研究与产品团队，结合了初创公司的速度和 Amazon 的规模与资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are really focused on building knowledge work agents that can perceive, reason, and act in a variety of different environments to complete real-world tasks.
zh: 我们真正专注于构建知识工作智能体，它们能够在各种不同的环境中感知、推理和行动，以完成真实世界的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our offices are in San Francisco and Boston.
zh: 我们的办公室在旧金山和波士顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got a few other talks going on throughout the week.
zh: 本周我们还有一些其他的演讲在进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a booth at the Expo, so stop by to collect some swag, meet some folks from the team, and hear some of the talks there.
zh: 我们在 Expo 有一个展位，欢迎过来领取一些纪念品，认识团队的一些成员，听听那里的一些演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to share a bit about our approach and how we think about agents.
zh: 接下来我想分享一点我们的方法，以及我们如何看待智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Across three different ways.
zh: 从三个不同的方面来讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first is around collaboration.
zh: 第一个是关于协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we really think about building agents that are teammates much more than just a black box.
zh: 我们真正想构建的智能体是队友，而不仅仅是一个黑盒。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we say teammates, we really want an agent that can understand what our goal is, our objective is, and can share how they're thinking about achieving that goal.
zh: 当我们说队友时，我们是希望智能体能够理解我们的目标、我们的目的是什么，并且能够分享它是如何思考去实现那个目标的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then...
zh: 然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: Grounding all of that in actual customer use cases.
zh: 把所有这些都锚定在实际的客户用例上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we work very, very closely with a large number of customers to really help ground all the work that we're doing with agents.
zh: 所以我们与大量客户非常非常紧密地合作，真正让我们在智能体方面所做的全部工作都有现实依据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second is around perception.
zh: 第二个是关于感知。

speaker: Unknown
en: So agents need to understand their environment.
zh: 智能体需要理解它们的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us, because it's a perception-based agent, the environment spans multiple devices.
zh: 对我们来说，因为这是基于感知的智能体，环境跨越多种设备。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started with browsers last year, but you can imagine any visual screen is an environment for our agent to carry out knowledge work in.
zh: 我们去年从浏览器开始，但你可以想象，任何可视化的屏幕都是我们智能体开展知识工作的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: So mobile devices and also computer use is the other one.
zh: 所以移动设备，另外还有计算机使用（computer use）是另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the third one is reliability.
zh: 第三个是可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a great customer quote that said, if my agent works 50% of the time, it doesn't work at all.
zh: 我们有一条很棒的客户引言说：如果我的智能体只有 50% 的时间能正常工作，那它就完全不能用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because you're either not going to run it at all, or if you do run it, you're going to end up debugging it and spending all this time, and you're going to basically do away with all the gains that you're getting from that agent.
zh: 这是因为你要么根本不会去运行它，要么如果你运行了，你最终会陷入调试并花费所有这些时间，而你基本上会把从这个智能体获得的所有收益都抵消掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we spend a lot of time building and training our models in simulated environments for reinforcement learning.
zh: 因此，我们花费大量时间在模拟环境中构建和训练我们的模型，用于强化学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, a lot of those are based on real-world use cases, which we get from not only our external customers, but a lot of internal Amazon teams that are carrying out a lot of knowledge work.
zh: 同样，其中很多都是基于真实世界的用例，这些用例不仅来自我们的外部客户，也来自许多正在进行大量知识工作的 Amazon 内部团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with that backdrop, I want to talk about the first product that we shipped last year.
zh: 有了这个背景，我想谈谈我们去年发布的第一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Amazon Nova Act.
zh: 那就是 Amazon Nova Act。

speaker: Unknown
en: is a first-class AWS service that allows developers to build and run reliable browser-based workflows at scale.
zh: 它是一个一等公民的 AWS 服务，允许开发者大规模地构建和运行可靠的基于浏览器的工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: So using natural language, you can drive a browser workflow to populate a browser, navigate, search with it, fill out forms, and call a human in the loop if you need a human for a expense report approval or if you get stuck or other things like that.
zh: 通过使用自然语言，你可以驱动一个浏览器工作流去操作浏览器、导航、用它进行搜索、填写表单，并且在需要人来处理费用报告审批，或者卡住了或其他类似情况时，调用人类介入（human in the loop）。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's kind of four primary use cases which we've seen customers adopt this for.
zh: 我们看到客户采用它主要有四类用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is form filling.
zh: 第一类是表单填写。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you have to do that at scale across a large number of different websites and you don't want to write a prompt for each single website or write like a deterministic script for each single site, you can use Nova Act for that.
zh: 如果你需要在大量不同的网站上大规模地做这件事，而你又不想为每个单独的网站写一个提示词，或者为每个单独的站点写一个确定性的脚本，你可以用 Nova Act 来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Search and extract if you want to do research and get data from a lot of different websites.
zh: 搜索和提取，如果你想进行研究并从很多不同的网站获取数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shopping and QA.
zh: 购物和 QA。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a bit more on what we launched.
zh: 再多说一点我们发布了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me just get through all these.
zh: 让我把这些都过一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a first-class AWS service.
zh: 它是一个一等公民的 AWS 服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you go into the AWS console, type in Nova Act, you will see Nova Act there.
zh: 所以如果你进入 AWS 控制台，输入 Nova Act，你会在那里看到 Nova Act。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from the console itself, you can see all of the trajectory.
zh: 从控制台本身，你可以看到所有的轨迹（trajectory）。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very easy way to see everything which your agent has done.
zh: 所以这是一种非常简单的方式，可以看到你的智能体做过的一切事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bounding boxes around all the elements which it's looking at, and it's trying to take actions on there.
zh: 它所看到的各个元素周围的边界框，然后它尝试对这些元素执行操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then behind the scenes, we have a custom computer use model, which is doing all of the inference there.
zh: 而在幕后，我们有一个定制的 computer use 模型，在那里进行所有的推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: This year we launched an MCP server as well as a skill, and you're gonna be using those in the workshop, and that's for your agents to be able to use Nova Act very easily, and then we've got human in the loop and tool use, and we also have a playground, so if you go to the Nova Act homepage, it's a no-code way to just see Nova Act in action there.
zh: 今年我们还推出了一个 MCP server 和一个 skill，你们在 workshop 中会用到它们，这是为了让你们的智能体能够非常轻松地使用 Nova Act，然后我们还有 human in the loop 和 tool use，我们还有一个 playground，所以如果你去 Nova Act 的主页，那是一种无代码的方式，可以直接看到 Nova Act 的实际运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, looking ahead, and the topic of today's workshop is perception agents.
zh: 现在，展望未来，今天 workshop 的主题是 perception agents。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, why do we feel there's a need for perception agents?
zh: 那么，为什么我们觉得需要 perception agents 呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for those of you who are not familiar with the term of computer use, that's basically the way for an agent to take an action on a computer screen, right?
zh: 对于那些不熟悉 computer use 这个术语的人来说，那基本上就是智能体在电脑屏幕上执行操作的方式，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you see a blue button in the right corner, and you tell your agent, hey, go click this blue button over here.
zh: 比如你在右角看到一个蓝色按钮，你告诉你的智能体，嘿，去点击那个蓝色按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very important, very powerful.
zh: 这非常重要，非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very important for automating workflows.
zh: 它对自动化工作流来说非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we feel that there's another half of that, which is the agent actually understanding what it's seeing on the screen itself.
zh: 但我们觉得还有另外一半，那就是智能体真正理解它在屏幕上看到的东西本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just using that as a sort of blind screen that it can just go and click on elements there.
zh: 而不仅仅是把它当作一个盲目的屏幕，只是去点击上面的元素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we really want this agent to be able to understand screen just like a human would, right?
zh: 我们真心希望这个智能体能够像人类一样理解屏幕，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So if I...
zh: 所以如果我……

speaker: Unknown
en: Showed someone an email client from like the late 90s that was like a Yahoo email client or Hotmail client or something which you've never seen before, you would probably be able to figure out how to send an email from that even though you've never used that client before because we've got this collective understanding of thousands and thousands of hours of using these screens that we kind of intuitively understand how to use these things and that's really where we're trying to get to with these agents.
zh: 给某人看一个像 90 年代末的电子邮件客户端，比如 Yahoo 邮件客户端或 Hotmail 客户端之类的你从未见过的东西，你很可能也能弄清楚如何从那里发送电子邮件，即使你以前从未用过那个客户端，因为我们积累了成千上万小时使用这些屏幕的集体理解，我们凭直觉就知道如何使用这些东西，而这正是我们希望通过这些智能体达到的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second one is these agents don't require APIs in order to work.
zh: 第二点是，这些智能体不需要 API 就能工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about a lot of knowledge work, it's a lot of humans using screens that just don't have APIs, and that's why there are people who are doing these things.
zh: 如果你想想很多知识工作，那其实是很多人在使用那些根本没有 API 的屏幕，这就是为什么需要人来做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want these agents to be able to carry out the same work across a variety of sites as well.
zh: 我们希望这些智能体能够在各种不同的网站上执行同样的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want the models to see the screens the same way that we do because that really facilitates the collaboration, right?
zh: 我们希望这些模型像我们一样看到屏幕，因为这真正促进了协作，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So rather than typing up paragraphs for what you want the agent to do on this screen and describing the screen, you can just point, click, and describe changes that you want.
zh: 这样一来，你不用打一大段文字来描述你想让智能体在这个屏幕上做什么、描述这个屏幕，你只需要指向、点击并描述你想要的更改。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what you're going to do in the workshop today is you're going to click on a couple elements and say, hey, I want to change the background to red, and that's it.
zh: 这就是你们今天在 workshop 中要做的事情，你们会点击几个元素，然后说，嘿，我想把背景改成红色，就这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you just have the agent go and do that.
zh: 然后你只需让智能体去完成它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to start with, we've open sourced two perception agent primitives, and you're gonna be using these in depth in the workshop today.
zh: 首先，我们已经开源了两个 perception agent 原语，你们今天会在 workshop 中深入使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is visual annotation.
zh: 第一个是 visual annotation。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what this lets you do is, on any webpage, you can point, click, and just describe changes that you wanna make.
zh: 它能让你做的是，在任何网页上，你可以指向、点击，然后描述你想要做的更改。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you're done with that, you click Export, and it exports out a JSON file with all the changes that you want and a prompt, which you can give to your coding agent along with that JSON file to say, hey, go and make these changes and do that.
zh: 完成之后，你点击 Export，它会导出一个 JSON 文件，包含你想要的所有更改以及一个 prompt，你可以把这个 JSON 文件连同 prompt 一起交给你的 coding agent，说，嘿，去做这些更改。

speaker: Unknown
en: So important to note, this has nothing to do with inference.
zh: 需要特别注意的是，这与推理完全无关。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is purely deterministic.
zh: 这纯粹是确定性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just outputs JSON.
zh: 它只输出 JSON。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not tied to any model or anything else like that.
zh: 它不依赖于任何模型或其他类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second part, the second primitive which we've launched is visual verification.
zh: 第二部分，我们推出的第二个原语是 visual verification。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about a site that you have, you've got certain CSS styles and designs which you want your site to adhere to.
zh: 如果你想想你拥有的一个网站，你有一些特定的 CSS 样式和设计，你希望你的网站遵循它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got different workflows which you want your site to support.
zh: 你有一些不同的工作流，你希望你的网站支持它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you have like a checkout flow or a login flow or something else, and you can describe those as Gherkin files.
zh: 也许你有一个 checkout 流程或登录流程之类的，你可以把它们描述成 Gherkin 文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can have visual verification, this skill, run by your coding agent against these design artifacts that you have, against these Gherkin files, and make sure that your site is adhering to those.
zh: 这样你就可以让 visual verification 这个 skill 由你的 coding agent 运行，对照你拥有的这些设计产物、这些 Gherkin 文件，确保你的网站遵循它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, this is something which you're going to use in the workshop today.
zh: 再说一次，这也是你们今天会在 workshop 中用到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, these are all open source, available today, and yeah, that's what we're going to do in the workshop.
zh: 再说一次，这些都是开源的，今天就可以使用，是的，这就是我们在 workshop 中要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think at this point I've spoken enough and I am going to hand it off to Shruti who is gonna kick us off on the workshop.
zh: 所以我觉得到这里我已经说得够多了，我现在把它交给 Shruti，她将带领我们开始 workshop。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, can you all hear me okay?
zh: 好了，大家都能听清我说话吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, welcome.
zh: 好的，欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, Amil, for that wonderful introduction to our Amazon AGI Labs and the products that we launched, we released earlier in May this year.
zh: 感谢 Amil 对我们的 Amazon AGI Labs 以及我们今年 5 月早些时候发布的产品所做的精彩介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as he mentioned, we are going to be doing hands-on workshop, but hands-on on whatever we release, the UI and the visual annotator and the visual verification.
zh: 正如他所说，我们将要进行动手 workshop，动手实践我们发布的东西，UI、visual annotator 和 visual verification。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a short demo here, but before we dive into the demo, I just want all of you to step into this role play here.
zh: 我这里有一个简短的 demo，但在深入 demo 之前，我只是想让大家先代入这个角色扮演。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just bear with me.
zh: 请稍等我一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So imagine you are a front-end engineer and you are building a web application.
zh: 想象你是一名前端工程师，你正在构建一个 web 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a design team and you are taking inspirations.
zh: 你有一个设计团队，你在从中获取灵感。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have this Figma files that you are building against.
zh: 他们有这些 Figma 文件，你是参照它们来构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are also collaborating with a sister team that they want to put in a piece of their information on the web page that you are building.
zh: 你还在和一个姐妹团队协作，他们想在你们正在构建的网页上放入他们的一块信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you are, if you think about it, that you have the designs, you'd probably take like four to five weeks to like build the designs and build everything code base and actually build that website.
zh: 所以如果你想一想，你拿到了设计稿，你可能需要大概四到五周的时间来构建设计、构建整个代码库，并真正把那个网站建出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, in the third week or fourth week around that time of your building process, you actually think, oh, maybe I should go back and verify if this looks fine, if everything looks okay with the rest of the team, and you are constantly collaborating, right?
zh: 现在，到了第三周或第四周左右，也就是你构建过程的那个时间点，你实际上会想，哦，也许我应该回头验证一下这个看起来是否没问题，和团队其他人确认一切是否正常，而且你们是在不断协作的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you are checking if the work that you have done is something that is what you want to ship.
zh: 所以你是在检查你所完成的工作是否就是你想发布的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you send your code base to, you share the GitHub or however you are doing your GitLab or whatever you have your code in and they run there, this web server locally and they open up the website and they say, oh, this feels off.
zh: 所以你把你的代码库发给,你分享 GitHub 或者不管你是用 GitLab 还是把代码放在哪里,他们在那里本地运行这个 web 服务器,他们打开网站然后说,哦,这感觉不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: The heading should be probably not.
zh: 标题应该可能不要。

speaker: Unknown
en: In red, I want to switch it back to something.
zh: 红色,我想换回某种颜色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they provide these feedbacks.
zh: 然后他们提供这些反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably they will do it in a Slack message or in a shared doc, for example.
zh: 很可能他们会通过一条 Slack 消息或者一个共享文档来提供,比如。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once you get those feedback on your website, you would then go over one of them, you'll disagree, agree to some of them, come to a middle ground and finalize, this is the feedback you want to incorporate.
zh: 然后一旦你在你的网站上收到这些反馈,你就会逐条过一遍,你会不同意一些、同意一些,折中一下然后确定下来,这就是你想要采纳的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to go through all of them and one by one and then start making the changes.
zh: 你必须把所有反馈一条一条过一遍,然后开始做修改。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now with coding agents, I guess it will take maybe over...
zh: 现在有了编码智能体,我想这可能需要大概……

speaker: Unknown
en: Which used to take maybe a week or it can reduce to maybe a few days.
zh: 这原本可能要花一周,现在可以缩减到大概几天。
